Intent

INTENT-01

Intent

CallerRepository maintainers and the existing codeArbiter feature/sprint authoring and execution workflows.
OutcomeProduce and consume consistent, reviewable, branded HTML specs and implementation plans through one Go helper without expanding public commands or persistent agent context.
ProblemSpecifications and implementation plans have useful prompt guidance but lack a shared mechanically enforced content, identity and mutation contract.
Source refs
  • SRC-21
Top

Scope

SCOPE-01

Scope

StatementAdd one shared Go artifact engine for canonical HTML specifications and implementation plans.
SCOPE-02

Scope

StatementMake behavioral criteria, plan tasks, relationships and lifecycle state typed and symbol-addressable.
SCOPE-03

Scope

StatementIntegrate existing feature/sprint, planning, TDD, execution, resume, context injection and farm consumers without adding public discovery surface.
SCOPE-04

Scope

StatementProvide safe mutation, revision checks, digest-bound stale detection and policy-preserving approval/acceptance records.
SCOPE-05

Scope

StatementDeliver offline human-readable branding, selective reads, legacy migration, native-platform packaging and verification.
Top

Non goals

NG-01

Non goals

StatementNo new /ca:spec, /ca:plan or other slash commands; no new always-registered agent tools, agents, or top-level skills.
NG-02

Non goals

StatementNo conversion of open-tasks, done-tasks, tickets, ADR bodies, audit logs, project decomposition plans or farm runtime JSON into the new canonical schema.
NG-03

Non goals

StatementNo database, resident daemon, browser editor, MCP server, generic artifact-plugin system or model-powered binary.
NG-04

Non goals

StatementNo replacement of existing user/SMARTS authorization, review, TDD, commit or branch-governance authorities.
NG-05

Non goals

StatementNo assertion that structured links prove intent completeness, that a digest authenticates an approver, or that HTML is empirically superior to Markdown.

Approach

APPROACH-01

Approach

Binding decision refs
  • DEC-01
  • DEC-02
  • DEC-03
  • DEC-04
  • DEC-10
  • DEC-11
ChoiceUse one file-based Go engine with separate typed spec and plan schemas, one authoritative embedded model per HTML file, deterministic rendering, and existing governed execution interfaces.
TradeoffAdds binary packaging and format-aware consumers, but removes free-form HTML construction and duplicated criteria identities. No database or always-registered tools are added.

Top

Decisions

DEC-01

Interaction surface

Authorityproposed
ChoiceUse existing governed EXEC/Bash tools and existing feature/sprint/plan routines. Load a small artifact-protocol leaf only when those routines need it.
RationaleThe proposed human-facing command only duplicated create/read/edit convenience already reachable in existing workflows.
DEC-02

First release boundary

Authorityproposed
ChoiceShip specs and implementation plans together; preserve all downstream consumers in the same rollout.
RationalePlan criteria references, execution state and resume are part of the first complete behavioral path.
DEC-03

Canonical representation

Authorityproposed
ChoiceOne HTML file per artifact, containing one authoritative JSON model and a deterministic static rendering.
RationaleNo editable JSON/Markdown sidecar; temporary request files and derived farm projections are explicitly non-authoritative.
DEC-04

Semantic ownership

Authorityproposed
ChoiceSpecs own criteria; plans reference them and own tasks. Evidence/approval sources remain owned by current governance.
RationaleAvoid independently rewritten acceptance ledgers and a second approval system.
DEC-05

Identity and integrity

Authorityproposed
ChoiceImmutable artifact/record IDs; separate document revision, normative digest and full model digest.
RationaleCosmetic changes and task status updates must not masquerade as requirement changes; actual contract changes must not retain approval.
DEC-06

Change concurrency

Authorityproposed
ChoiceDocument-level compare-and-swap with a writer lock and full-model hash; no automatic fine-grained merges in v0.1.0.
RationaleSequential revisions alone do not distinguish divergent branches or hand edits. A lock plus hash check prevents cooperating writers from losing updates.
DEC-07

Stale execution

Authorityproposed
ChoiceA changed spec or normative plan blocks new dispatch. Explicit reviewed rebind conservatively marks prior task evidence stale.
RationaleDo not carry ACCEPTED state across a changed contract by assuming a dependency graph proves unaffectedness.
DEC-08

Drafts and previews

Authorityproposed
ChoicePermit structurally valid partial drafts. A draft plan may be produced explicitly for review, but cannot execute until its spec and plan approvals are current.
RationaleThis package is a requested planning preview, not an exception to implementation gates.
DEC-09

Readable delivery

Authorityproposed
ChoiceSelf-contained static HTML is the canonical output in v0.1.0; use one renderer/style source, embedded per file.
RationaleRemoves broken local assets and the need for an extra save-as-single-file command. Runtime branding changes do not affect normative hashes.
DEC-10

Trust boundary

Authorityproposed
ChoiceTreat repository spec/plan text and commands as untrusted data. The binary never executes verification commands or model text.
RationaleExisting governed execution performs tests; a file-local approval record is a workflow attestation, not cryptographic identity proof.
DEC-11

Native distribution

Authorityproposed
ChoicePackage reviewed binaries; end users do not install Go or fetch dependencies during artifact operations.
RationalePin build inputs. Report native tested cells separately from cross-compiled artifacts; preserve existing native-platform support before default rollout.
DEC-12

Task granularity

Authorityproposed
ChoiceBound tasks by a verifiable concern, exact paths, dependencies and observable completion; do not invent a universal 2–5-minute duration.
RationaleThe current task-duration rule is a workflow heuristic, not evidence of an optimal plan schema. This release changes that wording explicitly.

Sections

SEC-INTENT

Intent and release boundary

Blocks

Make codeArbiter’s specifications and implementation plans consistent enough for machines to validate and pleasant enough for people to review. The agent writes domain content; a shared Go binary owns the two schemas, identity, selective extraction, safe mutation and rendering.

The caller is the existing codeArbiter feature/sprint workflow, not a new command or a new agent. The human continues to request a feature and review the resulting spec and plan through the current workflow. The files can also be opened directly in a browser.

References: SRC-04

This specification and its companion plan are populated reference outputs of the proposed format. They are DRAFT, not approved, and were generated by the bundled reference renderer, not a completed Go implementation. The user explicitly requested a planning preview; all implementation tasks remain PENDING.

Release measureRequired outcome
Public command and agent discoveryZero new slash commands, top-level skills, agent registrations or persistent agent-tool definitions.
Canonical artifact kindsBoth specification and implementation plan, with mutual integration rather than two unrelated renderers.
Completion of the changeExisting entry → spec approval → plan → bounded task execution → review → resume/commit consumes the new format.
Research claimEvidence-informed contract records; no claim that this full schema has won a comparative agent benchmark.

Review revision 2 uses reference schema 0.2.0 and renderer 0.2.0 because the unpublished reference schema changed incompatibly. The proposed first codeArbiter product release is still v0.1.0. Document revision, schema version and product release are independent. This is not a released format upgrade or an approved implementation.

SEC-BASELINE

Observed baseline and corrections

Blocks

The reviewed baseline is main at 45a17319f9ffda327cbdf3f3d40849bae8e920c0. The following are targeted source findings, not a claim that every repository file has been audited. The implementation plan begins with a consumer-closure inventory.

Current sourceObserved behaviorRequired correction
brainstormingProvides meaningful section and review guidance but writes Markdown directly.Keep the reasoning workflow; replace document construction with typed operations.
writing-plansExtracts criteria and allocates AC identifiers later.Allocate identities in the spec; plans retain qualified references and a source digest.
writing-plans coverage gateCalled bijection, but each side may reference multiple records.Name and implement bidirectional coverage. Many-to-many is valid; it is not a mathematical bijection.
TDDAlready permits one or more tests per obligation.Do not require exactly one physical test per criterion.
feature / executing-plansResume is driven by non-ACCEPTED plan tasks.Retain accepted tasks only when bound evidence and contract identity are still current.
_intentlib / _readinjectlibDepend on Markdown shape or .md discovery.Add format-aware consumers; never interpret unread HTML as an empty successful check.
References: SRC-01 SRC-02 SRC-03 SRC-04 SRC-05 SRC-07 SRC-08
SEC-EVIDENCE

Evidence basis and its limits

Blocks
BasisAdopted practiceNot established
Contract-first test-generation studyCondition, guarantee, boundary and test-oracle fields.A universally superior feature-spec schema, HTML layout or implementation-plan schema.
TiCoderUse concrete expected examples to clarify intent before implementation.That agent-generated examples alone establish the correct user intent.
EARSPrefer explicit triggers/conditions and observable responses when the pattern fits.A requirement to make invariants, tables and interface contracts fit one sentence form.
Current codeArbiter workflowStable obligations, exact paths, dependency ordering, review and fresh verification.An experimentally optimal task duration or a proof of semantic completeness.
References: SRC-15 SRC-16 SRC-17 SRC-02 SRC-03

For this change, each acceptance criterion is the behavioral-contract record. It has a statement, relevant conditions, observable guarantees, concrete scenarios and a verification oracle. A criterion can require several tests. Applicability decisions are explicit; a precondition may not assume away an input or failure the feature is responsible for handling.

The plan schema is an engineering design adapted to this repository. Validate it through correctness and interoperability tests. A later controlled pilot should separate representation changes from richer contract content, track human repair effort and total tokens, and hold independent acceptance checks fixed. Do not market structural validation as proof of improved agent outcomes.

SEC-SURFACE

Interaction and context budget

Blocks

The internal binary is provisionally named ca-artifact. Its CLI is a subprocess protocol, not a registered /ca: command and not an additional agent tool catalog. Do not introduce a convenience /ca:spec command or a new top-level skill. Existing workflow source files receive a short pointer to one shared, on-demand protocol leaf.

Surfacev0.1.0 behavior
Existing human entry pointsRetain /feature and /sprint routing, approvals and checkpoints. Browser-opened files provide review without a new command.
Existing agent execution toolsInvoke the resolved binary through the already governed EXEC/Bash path. Do not reclassify general binary execution as inspection or grant a new bypass.
Protocol discoveryLoad only the operation help and schema fragment needed for the current action. Root help is an operation index, not every schema.
Prompt loadingDo not inject full schemas, full specs/plans, command documentation or all symbols into SessionStart, the system prompt or the global tool schema.
Binary absence / mismatchReturn an actionable install/version diagnostic. Do not silently revert new-format artifacts to free-form agent writes.
Cold install and legacy workLegacy repositories keep their existing behavior until the new capability is installed and enabled; no implicit migration.
References: SRC-04 SRC-12 SRC-14 
Existing /feature or /sprint
  → existing brainstorming / writing-plans / execution routine
  → on-demand artifact protocol instructions
  → existing governed execution tool
  → ca-artifact <operation> --request <bounded-file>
  → one canonical HTML artifact + bounded JSON response

The fixed global discovery surfaces must gain zero new entries. Existing active routines may change their instructions; the integration test compares their added bootstrap text and verifies that schemas/help are not eagerly loaded. Do not promise zero context cost for doing the work itself.

SEC-MODEL

Artifact model and ownership

Blocks
Field or recordSpecificationImplementation plan
Envelopeformat/schema version, kind, immutable artifact ID, slug, revision, integrity and presentation.Same envelope, separate kind schema.
Normative contentProblem/caller/outcome; scope/non-goals; selected approach; decisions; criterion contracts; governs; unresolved decisions.Exact spec ID and normative hash; goal; task definitions; dependencies; checkpoints; verification definitions and path scopes.
Criterion identityOwned here, including stable AC IDs and any scenario IDs.Qualified refs only. A rendered coverage matrix is derived, not a copied editable ledger.
Lifecycle / evidenceApproval and review attestations reference the exact normative digest and their existing authority source.Plan approval plus task execution state and evidence references. Definition changes and state changes are distinct.
Execution commandsVerification intent and oracle; no automatic execution.Structured argv, repo-relative cwd, expected exit and assertion. Shell text only where explicitly allowed by existing policy.
Canonical bytesSingle .codearbiter/specs/<slug>.html.Single .codearbiter/plans/<slug>.html.

The existing plans/01-architecture-breakdown.md and plans/02-phased-build-plan.md are project decomposition records, not feature implementation plans. Preserve them in Markdown. Detect artifact kind by an explicit format marker and validated model, not simply by its directory name.

Schema versions and document revisions are different. The spec has explicit intent, approach and constraint records, not just section headings. Local/user-request sources are supported without a public URL; an unborn Git repository uses a null baseline commit. A locally supplied logo does not require a Git blob ID. Draft records can retain missing fields as absent/null/empty and readiness reports those exact gaps; it must never invent content. All schema references resolve from the installed package, without network access.

The common envelope is deliberately small. Future taskboard, ticket and ADR types may reuse storage, presentation and identity mechanisms, but do not implement their schemas or lifecycle semantics now.

All sections in this reference remain in the conservative normative hash, including explanatory source notes. This can cause reapproval after explanatory edits; it does not silently exclude prose from the approved contract. Contextual reads therefore include every normative section, global constraint, binding decision and blocker, paged if necessary, rather than guessing which paragraph matters.

Ready criteria require a nonblank statement, explicit applicability, guarantees, at least one complete scenario, a verification oracle, intent links and applicable constraints. Ready plans require complete task/path/verification/dependency records. Structural drafts permit incomplete records, but any supplied ID or reference must still be syntactically valid and internally resolvable. All active must criteria require coverage; should/may criteria need either coverage or an explicit plan disposition with rationale. Binary checks establish presence and relationships, not correctness of natural-language intent.

SEC-IDENTITY

Symbols, selective reads and canonical hashing

Blocks

Artifact IDs remain stable across file renames. The resolver scans approved artifact locations and verifies the embedded ID; a path is a locator hint, not authority. More than one live candidate for an artifact ID, including a Git merge duplicate, yields AMBIGUOUS_ARTIFACT and blocks dependent execution. A filename move may update presentation locators and model hashes, but does not rewrite criterion identities or normative plan binding. Record IDs are immutable and not recycled; retirement leaves a rendered tombstone with a reason and optional replacement ref.

Each addressable record is rendered once inside a generated CA:BEGIN / CA:END marker pair and an element carrying the same ID. Extract the model by ID, not by line number, heading text, array offset or marker-only heuristics. The HTML parser validates marker correspondence and nested pairing; user strings never become trusted markup.

<!-- CA:BEGIN:AC-009 -->
<article id="AC-009" data-ca-symbol="AC-009" data-ca-kind="criterion">
  ... generated content ...
</article>
<!-- CA:END:AC-009 -->

Go html/template strips literal HTML comments. Emit structural marker comments through a small trusted writer accepting only validated identifiers; escape all ordinary content. The reference renderer includes markers so their preservation is testable.

References: SRC-18
Read modeResult
outlineIDs, types, titles and dependency hints only; no automatic full-body dump.
read exactOne complete requested record with document identity and freshness; no dependent bodies.
read contextualThe record plus required spec constraints, linked criteria, task dependencies, open blockers and current approval status.
oversized contextual closureA paged manifest and explicit incomplete=true; no half-record truncation. Execution remains blocked until required context is obtained.
cursorBound to artifact ID and model hash. A changed artifact returns STALE_CURSOR rather than continuing a mixed-revision response.

normative_sha256 is SHA-256 over the JCS-compatible projection {format_version, kind, schema_version, artifact_id, normative}. model_sha256 covers the complete model except integrity. A writer requires both expected revision and expected model hash. The hashing profile accepts strings, booleans, null, arrays, objects and safe integers; reject duplicate keys, invalid Unicode, floats and out-of-range integers in v0.1.0. UTF-16 key ordering and canonical string serialization are covered by conformance vectors.

References: SRC-19

Presentation and execution status are excluded from the normative hash but included in the model hash. A new logo cannot invalidate requirements approval, but is still a guarded file mutation. A changed requirement invalidates the spec binding used by every plan without needing to eagerly rewrite those plans. Hash identity is not authentication.

A contextual-read cursor pins a dependency vector, not only the requested plan hash: artifact IDs and full model hashes for the plan, bound spec, and all fetched governing records or approval receipts. Recheck the vector before every page and before execution; a changed spec/approval while the plan is unchanged is STALE_CURSOR. A parsed file alone is not a validated read. Every outline/read checks supported schema, digests, marker/DOM correspondence and rendered-view consistency. Inspection cannot confer execution eligibility.

No receipt can prove that a model understood the returned context. context_complete reports deterministic record inclusion at the pinned snapshot only. Exact reads explicitly report context_complete=false. Before dispatch the coordinator must gather the complete required manifest; omitting a globally applicable section is not an optimization.

SEC-PROTOCOL

Internal operation contract

Blocks
Operation familyDefined behavior
describe / outline / read / validate / diffRead-only, bounded outputs. Validation distinguishes structural validity, ready-for-review, authority attestation and execution eligibility.
spec.create / plan.createCreate a new artifact without overwriting. Normal plan creation binds an approved spec; explicit draft-preview mode is non-executable.
applyTyped atomic batch: add/update/retire/reorder known record kinds. Targets immutable IDs, never arbitrary HTML/JSON-pointer patches.
record-approval / record-task-stateRestricted workflow transitions with exact hashes and evidence refs. Never fields writable by ordinary apply.
plan.rebindExplicitly bind a reviewed plan to a changed spec; present changes, invalidate affected approval and conservatively stale previous acceptances.
import / cutover / recoverReviewable legacy conversion, explicit canonical switch, recover interrupted file replacement/cutover without inventing state.
render / repairRender deterministically. Repair reports model-versus-view drift and preserves the original before an explicit approved replacement. No browser editing.

Use one bounded request file or JSON stdin, never embed domain prose in a shell command line. The wrapper constructs argv directly where supported; otherwise use the host’s existing quoting/execution contract. Responses are one JSON object on stdout; diagnostic logs go to stderr. No ANSI decorations or embedded instruction prompts in machine responses.

{
  "protocol_version": "0.1.0",
  "operation": "apply",
  "artifact": ".codearbiter/specs/example.html",
  "expected_revision": 8,
  "expected_model_sha256": "1111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111",
  "changes": [{"op": "criterion.update", "id": "AC-009", "fields": {"title": "Reject stale writers"}}]
}
ExitMeaning / sample code
0Requested operation succeeded. Execution eligibility is a separate explicit field.
2Malformed request, invalid schema or unsupported version: INVALID_REQUEST / UNSUPPORTED_VERSION.
3Unknown artifact or symbol: NOT_FOUND.
4Stale revision/hash, cursor or busy writer: REVISION_CONFLICT / STALE_CURSOR / LOCK_BUSY.
5Gate not met: NOT_READY / STALE_SPEC / STALE_EVIDENCE / AUTHORITY_UNVERIFIED.
6Untrusted path, tampered representation or unsupported storage: PATH_REJECTED / RENDER_DRIFT / STORAGE_UNSUPPORTED.
7I/O failure or recovery needed: IO_ERROR / RECOVERY_REQUIRED.

Default read responses are capped at 32 KiB UTF-8 and request input at 1 MiB; a canonical file is capped at 8 MiB and a user logo at 256 KiB. These are proposed engineering bounds, not research-derived optima. The smallest unit is a complete record; an oversized single record returns a size diagnostic and a bounded field manifest, not a truncated contract. A declared, operator-approved cap change is not an unbounded override.

The request cap is 1 MiB before parsing; the file cap is 8 MiB before parsing, nesting is at most 64, and symbol count at most 8192. The default response cap is 32 KiB. A ready record must fit a 12 KiB canonical-record cap; larger drafts are allowed but not ready until reviewed decomposition. Do not paginate through half a criterion. Return OUTPUT_TOO_LARGE with a bounded field manifest and required byte count. Fixed caps are engineering choices, not research optima. Strict field-level draft patches can fill one incomplete record over multiple requests.

Model construction, rendering and schema inspection are not approval operations. Authority transitions consume the existing governance-owned receipt by exact locator and digest, not request-supplied statements about approval. The same-user threat model remains cooperative: a local actor able to rewrite both artifacts and policy-owned receipts is outside this mechanism. Do not claim a secure approval boundary from a special operation name or the Go executable alone.

SEC-LIFECYCLE

Approval, task state and stale evidence

Blocks

Allow DRAFT → READY → APPROVED → SUPERSEDED, with readiness derived from validation and approval checked against the exact normative hash. DRAFT may be incomplete; READY requires no unresolved blocking decision and complete applicable contracts/relationships. The existing feature user gate and sprint SMARTS decision remain the policy authorities. A document record reports workflow attestation and its source; it is not a cryptographic proof of a human identity.

References: SRC-01

The workflow adapter records approved content only after its existing authorization and audit steps. Generic apply cannot create approvals, set APPROVED, mark tasks ACCEPTED or fabricate evidence. If a source is unavailable or cannot be bound, report AUTHORITY_UNVERIFIED and block execution rather than turning a self-declared flag into authority. Existing same-user filesystem limitations are explicit; this is not a sandbox against an arbitrary local writer.

Task statePermitted meaning
PENDINGDefined work, not yet dispatched. This is every task in the companion draft plan.
IN_PROGRESSDispatched under a current contract; never equivalent to accepted.
BLOCKEDCannot advance; contains a reason and relevant decision/dependency references.
REVIEWAuthoring done; review or fresh verification still pending.
ACCEPTEDCurrent spec/task identities, fresh verification and existing spec/quality review gates are all satisfied.
STALEHistorical evidence is retained but no longer sufficient for current execution/resume.

Acceptance evidence identifies spec/plan/task normative hashes, verification invocation and outcomes, review receipts, and a verification-input fingerprint. Do not hash the mutable plan HTML, audit ledger or evidence receipt into the fingerprint that the acceptance write itself changes. Use a versioned verification-input manifest: source/test/config/toolchain inputs, membership for covered directories (including newly added or deleted files), and normative projections for governed spec/plan inputs. Exclude only exact, independently validated control-state/evidence outputs and presentation fields. Never exclude the whole .codearbiter directory. A policy/config/test edit remains an input change; HEAD alone never proves dirty-worktree freshness.

On resume, first validate authority, spec/plan bindings and outstanding recovery records. Within one active checkpoint scope, a dependency in REVIEW with successful spec review and fresh task verification may unblock the next task provisionally. Across scopes, dependencies must be ACCEPTED and applicable evidence current. REVIEW is never completion, export eligibility or release authority. IN_PROGRESS after interruption returns reconciliation; verified REVIEW work can resume within its same scope after revalidation. Never restart approved framing merely because verification must be rerun.

References: SRC-04 SRC-05 SRC-06

Ordinary task state changes do not mutate the plan’s normative definition. A normative plan edit invalidates plan approval. Rebinding to a changed specification is explicit and does not silently regenerate wording, dependencies, verification commands or historical acceptance.

Each checkpoint is an execution scope. Scope entry validates external dependencies and records the starting tree. Tasks move PENDING → IN_PROGRESS → REVIEW after task-level spec compliance and fresh verification. Same-scope dependencies may use REVIEW only on that recorded tree lineage. After all members reach REVIEW, reverify the entire scope against one final verification-input fingerprint and run the existing combined-diff quality review. accept-scope atomically records acceptance for all members or none, through the recovery-aware authority adapter. Failed review returns affected tasks to work and invalidates dependent provisional results. This explicitly repairs the old accepted-dependency/whole-scope-review ordering conflict without skipping quality review.

References: SRC-06

A later source change makes applicable verification stale; it does not erase historical completion or force reimplementation. Revalidation reruns the relevant checks and binds a new receipt to current inputs. A normative spec/plan change instead requires reviewed rebind/reapproval. State-only, presentation-only and exact evidence-output writes leave the verification-input fingerprint unchanged. Final checkpoint and commit handoff still require all applicable checks current at the final snapshot.

Checkpoint ordering is explicit. A checkpoint cannot depend on a later checkpoint, and task selection cannot cross an unaccepted earlier checkpoint. Bootstrap tasks may define the format, but implementing the engine must not depend on the engine already enforcing its own plan: use the current approved workflow for this one bootstrap implementation, then exercise the new path in isolated fixtures before cutover.

SEC-STORAGE

Storage, safety and rendering

Blocks

For each mutation: resolve the repository and trusted artifact path; acquire a bounded per-artifact writer lock; read and validate the current file; compare revision and model hash under that lock; validate the proposed complete model; render to a same-filesystem temporary file; verify the staged bytes; replace through a platform-tested primitive; then release the lock. Lock contention returns a conflict; never automatically steal a lock based only on wall-clock age.

Guarantee no lost update among cooperating writers and no partial canonical HTML after a supported single-file replacement. Distinguish process interruption from power-loss durability. Native platform tests and an explicit recovery record must support any durability claim. Do not assume ordinary rename gives identical Windows and Unix guarantees. Network filesystems and mixed-runtime shared working trees are not promoted by this feature.

Approve/cutover operations may touch an artifact plus an audit/index record. Do not claim a multi-file transaction from a single-file rename. Stage a bounded intent/recovery record with exact old/new hashes; incomplete state blocks execution and exposes a read-only recovery report until reconciliation. Ordinary reads must not execute recovery or make hidden writes.

Reject traversal, absolute repository-escape paths, symlink/reparse-point escapes, ambiguous identifiers and unsafe asset references. Never trust a binary resolved from the target repository or arbitrary PATH. Trusted package resolution and its existing installation boundary select the executable. The binary does not make network requests, load remote schemas or run commands stored in a plan.

Render a real static document, with the retrieved codeArbiter logo by default. Repository branding may provide a display name and a local PNG/JPEG or strictly validated inert SVG. No remote images, executable SVG, scripts, arbitrary templates or stylesheet injection. Embed the sanitized result, CSS and model so the document is portable and works offline. Escape JSON for the HTML script-data context so a literal closing script tag cannot escape the model container.

References: SRC-13

Use semantic headings, keyboard-accessible native disclosure, visible record anchors, light-background body text and print rules. Test 390 px and 1440 px viewports, 200% text zoom, long identifiers and code blocks. Layout may scroll a code/table container horizontally, but no element may overlap or escape its container. No font files or external font dependencies are shipped.

Do not promise that every post-replacement I/O error means no mutation. Before replacement, validation/conflict failure leaves bytes unchanged. After replacement, an audit/receipt/fsync failure is COMMIT_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN or RECOVERY_REQUIRED and returns the operation ID plus known identities. Retries inspect the recovery record instead of blindly applying the mutation again. A bounded operation ID and old/new hashes distinguish an acknowledged repeat from a new request.

A model names only a supported, package-owned renderer version and stylesheet digest. Unknown renderers yield UNSUPPORTED_RENDERER, not RENDER_DRIFT or silent reformatting. Upgrades preserve old readers or require an explicit reviewed presentation migration. Git conflicts or competing model containers are invalid until reviewed resolution; never auto-merge array positions or mint replacement IDs to conceal conflicts.

Reference rendering must show actual obligation labels, blockers, tombstones and task states. It must not hard-code MUST, PENDING, zero accepted tasks or absence of open decisions. A displayed approval state is labeled recorded and authority-unverified until the coordinator checks the external authority source. Custom branding changes title and visible brand label as well as the logo; provenance remains available separately.

Consumer closure and compatibility

References: SRC-01 SRC-02 SRC-03 SRC-04 SRC-05 SRC-06 SRC-07 SRC-08 SRC-09

Farm JSON is a disposable execution projection, never a second editable plan. Model selection remains owned by dispatch. The first gate command is still the narrow behavioral test, and fresh red evidence must exist before farm authoring. Projecting a draft, stale or unapproved plan is rejected.

References: SRC-09

Small-lane inline mini-specs remain inline in this release because they do not currently create the full spec/plan file pair. This change does not silently expand ceremony. Historical records and whole-project decomposition documents remain readable and are excluded from blanket format validation.

Farm projection has two identities. The base binding covers canonical runtime JSON excluding only the allowed dispatch-time meta.model and meta.apiBaseUrl fields; it also pins spec/plan normative hashes, slice membership and ID mapping. Before any canary or dispatch side effect, validate the base and current source pair. Authorized model selection may fill only those fields. After selection, seal an execution receipt over the exact full runtime JSON bytes plus their selected-provider provenance. The runtime guard verifies that sealed receipt immediately before side effects. Any task/test/scope/command change invalidates the base; any later byte change invalidates the execution seal. The binary validates data but still does not run the farm.

References: SRC-22

The farm source guard must live at the actual existing dispatcher/preview execution boundary, not just in a Markdown instruction. T-001 inventories the canonical runtime paths; T-018 cannot dispatch until those exact source paths are added to its approved path set and the guard is implemented for canary and normal dispatch. Preserve the existing closed runtime schema and existing legacy farm eligibility policy; derived sidecar receipts are not editable planning authority.

SEC-MIGRATION

Migration, rollout and rollback

Blocks

Keep legacy reads during rollout. Import a selected feature spec and implementation plan into a review-only candidate pair. Capture original bytes/hashes, old status/AC numbering as provenance, unresolved mappings, and proposed stable IDs. Never infer approval or ACCEPTED evidence from uppercase words or checkboxes alone.

Show a semantic conversion report: preserved intent, mapped criteria/tasks, unresolved ambiguities, copied historical claims and newly required contract fields. Human or existing policy review supplies missing meaning. A source hash changed since preview blocks cutover. Completed legacy work does not automatically acquire verified evidence under the new format.

Switch the pair under a recovery-aware cutover record. Remove legacy live authority only after the new pair validates and the switch is reviewed. Preserve originals in version control or the exact migration backup, never two writable canonical copies. An interrupted switch is RECOVERY_REQUIRED, not a successful mixed-format execution state.

Rollback first stops dispatch. Before new-format mutations, restore the captured old pair through a reviewed revert. After new-format work exists, use an explicit loss report and reviewed reverse export/reconciliation; never just downgrade the binary or delete HTML. Retain evidence/history. No destructive migration is part of merely opening these reference files.

Rollout checkpointExit condition
0. Approve scopeSpec/plan pair and narrow architecture decision accepted through existing governance.
1. Reader and writer conformanceNew engine validates and round-trips both kinds with golden/adversarial fixtures; legacy reads remain unchanged.
2. Internal workflow pilotOne fixture project completes spec → plan → reviewed execution → interruption/resume and current-slice farm projection.
3. Native host evidenceSupported Windows, Linux and macOS cells pass real write/recovery and generated-adapter tests. Cross-compilation is not native proof.
4. Selected migrationReviewed pair migration, crash recovery and rollback demonstrated; no global mass conversion.
5. Default enablementConsumer-closure manifest and applicable repository gates pass; command/agent/tool catalogs remain unchanged.
SEC-REVIEW

Design review and unresolved work

Blocks

This is an author review of the proposed artifacts, not an independent code review. No implementation tests, host matrix runs, user approval or model-performance experiment are claimed.

Risk foundDisposition
New spec command adds redundant contextRemoved. No new public commands or persistent agent tools.
Spec-only migration strands plan readers and resumeSpecs and plans are one v0.1.0 rollout unit.
Shared-word coverage can appear complete on unread HTMLNew-format readers must validate kind/schema first; explicit relationships replace that heuristic.
A plan status can remain ACCEPTED after its contract changesNormative hash binding, stale state and pre-dispatch checks are mandatory.
HTML and embedded JSON can divergeDeterministic view check and explicit repair, never silent overwrite.
Revision-only CAS loses updates across divergent branchesRequire expected model hash plus revision and lock.
Single-file atomic write cannot atomically update an audit/indexRecovery-aware protocol explicitly covers multi-file transitions.
Persisted approval can be self-authoredAuthority provenance is reported honestly; generic editing cannot perform workflow transitions. This is not cryptographic authentication.
A complete traceability graph can encode the wrong intentRetain negative-completeness and independent review; links do not prove meaning.

The architecture remains a draft. The initial repository/authority/host inventory is a hard prerequisite before runtime integration; unresolved mappings must be raised through existing decision governance. No write, durability, authorization or agent-performance guarantee is claimed as implemented by these reference files. The review report records corrected defects and the tests actually run against the reference package.

Negative-completeness check: even if isolated record tests passed, an unchanged resume or farm consumer could still operate on the wrong contract. The integration, stale-evidence, farm and consumer-closure criteria below make that end-to-end behavior explicit.

The reference regression suite tests partial criteria/tasks, local sources and unborn repositories, open blockers, optional obligation labels, retired symbols, visible/model drift, mutated digests, wrong source-spec identity and invalid graph edges. Scope scheduling, multi-artifact cursors, evidence-input snapshots, farm seals and native write recovery are specified adversarial implementation scenarios; their Go/host tests have not run. The separate review reports enumerate actual reference tests and browser checks.
